note: The pinned sources of gen_x86sys.py. Trust chain (CLAUDE.md rule 7): documented Win32 (WDK 7.1 headers, MSDN), the Intel SDM, and Wine 9.0 under the owner's Wine rule. No other source. WDK mirror: fnv-nx-build tools/wdk71-headers (MANIFEST.json there records the ISO, cab and msi hashes). gen_x86sys.py checks the sha256 of every file it reads against this record.

sysinfo.origin: Wine 9.0 dlls/ntdll/unix/system.c (get_cpuinfo: CPUID bits to CPU_FEATURE_*, have_sse_daz_mode)

wineboot.origin: Wine 9.0 programs/wineboot/wineboot.c (CPU_FEATURE_* to ProcessorFeatures[PF_*] of the user shared data)

usd_mapping.origin: Wine 9.0 server/mapping.c (create_user_data_mapping: the section the features are written into)

wine.files_note: system.c, wineboot.c and mapping.c were read from the upstream tag wine-9.0; dlls/ntdll/unix/signal_i386.c of the same tag has the pinned sha256 of the mirror commit, which ties the tag to the mirror. Pin them in the mirror's MANIFEST when the mirror is next touched.

cpumodel.origin: the declared CPU's cpuid as data (CPUREF: verify/cpuref.json + verify/cpuid_model.json); lift/rt/cpumodel.c is generated from it, not a source

precedence: (1) documented Win32 for Windows 7 SP1 build 7601: MSDN and WDK 7.1
(2) Wine 9.0, only where it contradicts neither (1) nor the declared OS
(3) nothing else (ReactOS is not a source)

doc_gates.source: MSDN __fastfail intrinsic: fast fail is supported from Windows 8 (build 9200); Windows 7 SP1 is build 7601, so int 0x29 is not a fast-fail gate there. What the instruction does on build 7601 is not stated by MSDN: undecided

cpuref.origin: the declared CPU's identity (vendor_id GenuineIntel), CPUREF

sdm.title: Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual, Volume 3A: System Programming Guide, Part 1
sdm.terms: ASM-055 (OWNER 10, per the orchestrator): an MS term such as '32-bit flat mode' means what SDM vol. 3A 3.2.1 defines; ASM-055 was not present in verify/ASSUMPTIONS.json on claude/fnv-nx-clean or claude/port-nsw-un6t9s when read (2026-11-15), so the citation names it as the ruling and the registry entry is owed by the orchestrator
